brief.angle: A 100-page plain text document uses roughly the same context capacity as just 10 seconds of raw video frame grid patches.
brief.measure: Comparing text token count per page to image patch tokens across a short video sequence.
brief.calc: 100 pages * 500 words * 1.33 tokens/word = 66,500 tokens vs 10 seconds * 24 frames * 256 tokens/frame = 61,440 tokens.
brief.why_now: Explains why multimodal AI chat runs out of context much faster when processing video input.

spec.title: Text pages match ten seconds of video
spec.summary: Comparing text tokens to visual grid patches across identical capacity.

beats.say: One hundred pages of text equals ten seconds of video.
Both formats consume nearly identical token counts in models.
Text uses words translated into numbers.
One hundred pages hold fifty thousand words.
Word math yields sixty six thousand tokens.
Video uses frames split into grid patches.
Patch math yields sixty one thousand tokens.
The totals land within ten percent of each other.
Visual frames pack dense data faster than print.
Models process reading and seeing through identical math.
